tldr: Final architecture (2026-10-20, docs/architecture.md): Interface is a GitHub fork of Parallel Code (MIT) with about 25 changed upstream lines. Our own TypeScript packages live in this repo and ship into the app as one sha256-pinned bundle. A hub inside the app (MCP SDK v2, 127.0.0.1, a fresh token per agent launch) serves Parallel, Firecrawl, Octen and Context7 tools to every Claude Code, OpenCode and Muse agent the app starts. Keys stay in GNOME Keyring via secret-tool, and no CLI config file is edited. Stages: S1 the fork runs as our app; S2 hub in the app (0.1.0, the first usable release, proven by six tool calls); S3 terminal use and provider CLIs; S4 Continue in...; S5 limits and auto-switch. A weekly bot PR merges upstream. Dropped: the --mcp-config 'fix' (based on a refuted claim), add-mcp, 1MCP and mcp-proxy at runtime, CodexBar. Next: Muse and OpenCode spikes.
winner_and_grafts:
WINNER: thin-fork. It came first with the maintainability judge (29/40) and the safety judge (33/40), and its 86-point total beats core-first (79) and max-assembly (65). Max-assembly won only the delivery lens. Most of the delivery judge's adjustments below were adopted, so the thin fork keeps its fast first app (S1) and the hub reaches the app in S2.

KEPT FROM THIN-FORK:
- Two repos: this MIT repo with every OpenSpec change, and a GitHub fork, siddharth-0044/interface-desktop.
- Rule "add files, don't edit them": about 25 seam lines in hot files.
- A sha256-pinned core bundle unpacked into git-ignored dist-electron/. Re-checked today: upstream's build doesn't clean that folder, and build.files packs it. So the fork never touches package.json or the lockfile.
- A generated electron-builder config. A typed host contract with apiVersion. Fail-soft: without the bundle the app is plain Parallel Code.
- The hub in an Electron utilityProcess, keys via secret-tool (stdin confirmed in the local man page), per-launch revocable tokens, and the six-call S2 acceptance test.

REMOVED (relied on refuted facts):
- P3 and U1 assumed Parallel Code passes --mcp-config to OpenCode and custom agents. Verified false: canvas and coordinator MCP only run for claude, codex and copilot.
- U3 is retargeted from buildMcpLaunchArgs (refuted call graph) to a launch-contributor hook in pty.ts spawnAgent. That is the one path both SpawnAgent IPC and coordinator children go through.

GRAFTS:
1. Weekly merge-commit sync PR instead of rebase plus force-with-lease (core-first; maintainability and delivery judges). The mirror stays on main, our default branch is 'interface', and upstream PRs are cherry-picks onto the mirror.
2. scripts/check-seams in CI (max-assembly).
3. dependency-cruiser boundaries (core-first). Core imports no Electron and no MCP SDK. SDK v2 is used only in packages/hub. Key reading is allowed only in the hub and ifc run (safety judge's least-privilege idea, adapted).
4. jsonc-parser plus 'claude mcp' instead of add-mcp. Port only rulesync's Muse field mapping: keep the existing root key, write schema_version 1, use one optional flag (core-first; verification).
5. Official transcript exports first; continues is optional (core-first). Today's local checks confirmed 'opencode session export' and 'muse export'.
6. ifc packaged inside the rpm (max-assembly), deferred to S3. It runs on system node: upstream's own MCP server already uses 'command: node', so the rpm requires nodejs.
7. Keyless providers keep serving when the keyring is locked, plus a dependency register with pins and fallbacks (max-assembly).
8. Anti-spoofing: the seam deletes, then sets, INTERFACE_* in spawnEnv after buildPtySpawnEnv, so upstream's ENV_BLOCK_LIST isn't edited (maintainability judge's version of the core-first idea).
9. Pinned vendor installers with --skip-auth (core-first; the safety judge confirmed that Firecrawl's browser login writes plaintext credentials).
10. Write-only keys IPC (windows get hasKey only) and an honest threat model, including ptrace_scope 0 (core-first; safety judge).
11. Global sync by reference: Muse ${VAR}, OpenCode {file:}/{env:}, Claude headersHelper. Never a literal token (safety judge).
12. A spawn-env CI test and constant-time token compare (max-assembly).
13. Hub front on the SDK v2 Host, Origin and bearer helpers. Reject any Origin, no CORS, no SSE, checks before body parsing (safety judge, prompted by the mcp-proxy finding).
14. Billing guard at launch, not only in doctor (safety judge).
15. Electron fuses (safety judge). Re-checked today that upstream doesn't rely on ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE for its MCP server.
16. Key-to-host binding and absolute shim paths (safety judge).
17. Untrusted handoff briefs, from Waybill's rule.
18. One --mcp-config list next to upstream's canvas config, with fixtures for both argument orders (delivery judge; canvas is on for every fresh Claude spawn).
19. Explicit S2 acceptance. Global-sync fallback pulled into S2 for any CLI whose spike fails (delivery judge).
20. Canonical Muse 'mcpServers' with required:false, because this machine's settings.json uses mcpServers (delivery judge).
21. OpenCode entry with oauth:false and a Code Mode check (core-first).
22. 'fetch-core --local' plus a fork-side core-bump job, with no cross-repo token (maintainability judge).
23. A dev-prerequisites check for gcc-c++, make and rpm-build (delivery judge).

NEW FROM THIS PASS (read-only checks):
- Upstream already has a 'Chat is turned off for Claude Code' setting (disableClaudeUiMode, default false in src/store/core.ts). Turning off the Agent-SDK chat view is therefore a one-line default change. That view passes only one MCP config, so our hub never reaches it.
- GitHub docs: PRs opened by a workflow with GITHUB_TOKEN do get CI runs, but each run needs one maintainer approval click. The bot flow works without a PAT.
- muse --yolo disables approval and the sandbox. muse --provider echo exists for cheap spikes.

proposal.md:
- Remove the framing 'terminal-first, can be shipped before any GUI' and the 'macOS-only JOY' phrase (JOY now ships Linux builds, including a Fedora rpm).
- Say the hub is the engine of Interface Desktop and reaches agents per launch.
- Move 'Repository and delivery setup' to setup-dev-loop and 'Per-CLI adapters' to terminal-and-global-sync.
- Impact: no CLI config writes in this change. Dependencies are @modelcontextprotocol/server, /client and /node (Apache-2.0) and the secret-tool binary.

design.md:
- D1: TypeScript on the SDK v2 split packages. The downstream endpoint must speak the legacy protocol era: Muse advertises 2025-06-18 and OpenCode v2 defaults to 'legacy'. Use createMcpHandler, with versionNegotiation 'auto' toward providers.
- D2: secret-tool subprocess with the secret on stdin and attributes application=interface, kind=provider-key, provider=<id>. It sits behind a SecretStore split into reader and writer. No fallback store. Document @napi-rs/keyring pinned to {linux:{store:'secret-service'}} as the alternative.
- D3: paths become ~/.config/interface/hub.json and $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/interface/.
- D4: keep always-prefixed <provider>_<tool> names, with a 64-character limit and a hash fallback.
- D5: per-launch tokens, minted by the caller, registered with the hub and revoked on exit. Host allowlist; reject any request with an Origin header; no CORS; no SSE endpoint; constant-time compare; all checks before body parsing on every route. Default port 7337, with a free-port fallback.
- D6: replace the adapters with LaunchPlanner.plan(ctx) -> {args, env, files, cleanup}.
  - Claude: a 0600 file merged into the existing --mcp-config list.
  - OpenCode: --standalone plus OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT, deep-merged with any existing value. Use the v2 mcp.servers.interface shape with oauth:false; the spike decides codemode.
  - Muse: -c mcpServers.interface with canonical type, url and headers, required:false, and header ${INTERFACE_HUB_AUTH}.
  - Skip shells, Docker tasks, unknown CLIs and globally synced CLIs. Add the billing guard and the INTERFACE_* spoof guard.
- D7: the caller hosts the hub (an Electron utilityProcess in the app, ifc later), with lazy connect and backoff.
- D8: moves to setup-dev-loop.
- Catalog: Parallel search (keyless OK) and task (same key); Firecrawl Bearer, with a warning when keyless; Octen x-api-key; Context7 optional Bearer. Each key only goes to its catalog host. Keyless providers keep working when the keyring is locked.
- Risks: replace the native-module risk with the spike risks.

specs/mcp-hub/spec.md:
- Keep the provider, aggregation, naming, failing-provider and diagnostics requirements.
- MODIFY 'Hub endpoint requires a local access token' to per-launch tokens. Scenarios: token rejected after the agent exits; foreign Host rejected; any Origin rejected; OPTIONS and /sse rejected.
- REMOVE 'Supported CLIs are pointed at the hub' and 'CLI config edits are safe and reversible'; they move to terminal-and-global-sync.
- ADD 'Agents get the hub per launch'. Scenarios: launch plans match the fixtures for each CLI; no CLI config file changes; shells and Docker are skipped.
- ADD 'Keys only reach their own provider host', 'Keyless providers keep working when the keyring is locked' and 'Claude launches drop Anthropic API variables by default'.

user_decisions.question: What is the final product name?
options: Keep 'Interface' (credited as based on Parallel Code)
user_decisions.recommendation: Decide before the S1 release; keep 'Interface' if nothing better comes up
user_decisions.why: The name goes into the appId, rpm name, keyring entries and update feed. Changing it after the first release breaks updates and stored keys.

user_decisions.question: How should the fork follow upstream Parallel Code?
options: Weekly bot PR merged with a merge commit
Rebased patch stack with a weekly force-push (original thin-fork plan)
user_decisions.why: Nothing is rewritten under friends' open PRs or clones, and 'gh repo sync' and the GitHub UI keep working. With about 25 changed lines and PATCHES.md, the patches stay visible.

user_decisions.question: Which keyring backend?
user_decisions.recommendation: secret-tool behind the SecretStore interface (revises design D2)
user_decisions.why: It ships in Fedora's libsecret, needs no native build or Electron packaging tricks, accepts the secret on stdin, and is easy to check from a terminal.

user_decisions.question: Who runs the hub?
options: The app now, with an optional systemd service in S3
user_decisions.recommendation: The app now, with an optional systemd service in S3
user_decisions.why: Nothing extra to install for 0.1.0, and the app only ever talks to a hub it started itself. Terminal users can opt in later.

user_decisions.question: Should upstream's Claude chat view be off by default?
options: Off by default (flip upstream's existing disableClaudeUiMode setting, one line)
user_decisions.recommendation: Off by default; users can turn it back on in Settings
user_decisions.why: The safety review flagged Anthropic's policy on third-party Agent-SDK products. Also, per-launch hub injection doesn't reach that view, because it passes only one MCP config file.

user_decisions.question: What should the billing guard do?
options: Remove ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and CLAUDE_CODE_USE_* from Claude launches by default, with a per-agent opt-in
user_decisions.recommendation: Remove by default, show a notice, and allow a per-agent opt-in
user_decisions.why: A stray ANTHROPIC_API_KEY silently moves Claude Code from your subscription to pay-per-use billing, and this project exists to use subscriptions.

user_decisions.question: Where should Muse quota data come from in S5?
user_decisions.recommendation: Only limit messages, until Meta documents a usage API
user_decisions.why: CodexBar uses Muse's login token to mint a key through an undocumented Meta endpoint, which is a terms-of-service grey area.

unverified: Muse 1.4.11 accepts '-c mcpServers.interface=<JSON object>' for a new server name, with a whole-value ${INTERFACE_HUB_AUTH} header, and refuses it when a same-named global entry exists. Spike with --provider echo.

OpenCode 2.0.32 applies a per-launch OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT only with --standalone, standalone sessions appear in the normal session list, and prefixed hub tools work under Code Mode (codemode defaults to true).
Claude Code 2.1.304 loads two configs given in one --mcp-config list (ours next to Parallel Code's canvas file) without prompts, and canvas tools keep working.
Claude Code, OpenCode and Muse send no Origin header to an HTTP MCP server. The reject-any-Origin rule depends on this.

An Electron utilityProcess can run the hub bundle from the packaged app, and the Electron fuses (runAsNode, NODE_OPTIONS and inspect turned off) break nothing, including auto-update. Upstream's own MCP server runs with system node, which suggests upstream doesn't use runAsNode.
The per-launch token reaches the hub over MessagePort before the agent's first request. If not, switch to signed tokens the hub can check without a registration step.
A locked GNOME keyring shows an unlock prompt when secret-tool runs from the app or from a systemd user service, and such a service can reach the Secret Service.
electron-builder builds our rpm on an Ubuntu runner with rpm installed, the rpm 'depends' list (libsecret, nodejs) works, and AppImage auto-update works from our fork's releases.
The rebranded app uses its own userData folder and single-instance lock, so it can run next to an installed Parallel Code.

Agent sandboxes let PATH shims reach D-Bus (Muse's sandbox is on unless --yolo). Vendor skills call bare parallel-cli and firecrawl from PATH. Parallel's skill-installer command is unknown, and so is whether 'firecrawl-cli init --all --skip-auth' stores nothing.
The output of 'muse export' and 'opencode session export' is enough for handoff briefs, and continues can still read current Claude Code sessions.
Claude's StopFailure hook detail identifies rate limits. What OpenCode and Muse print when they hit a usage limit is unknown, and cezar has no Muse patterns.
Claude user-scope MCP entries accept headersHelper, which global sync needs to reference the token instead of writing it.
Docker tasks on Linux may reach the host's 127.0.0.1 when run with --network host (an upstream code comment in electron/mcp/config.ts says so). Untested, so Docker tasks are skipped.
Orca's Muse preset details (--trust-workspace, prompt via stdin) still apply to Muse 1.4.11.
This pass did not re-read Anthropic's policy on third-party Agent-SDK products; it relies on the safety judge's summary.
Effort estimates per stage are guesses for a beginner building with AI coding agents.
